```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Model fits need CmdStan and take a few minutes. They run only when
# PNEUMOALLOC_VIGNETTE_FITS=true, e.g. when building the pkgdown site.
run_fits <- identical(Sys.getenv("PNEUMOALLOC_VIGNETTE_FITS"), "true")
```

## The problem

In carriage surveys a child can carry several pneumococcal serotypes at
once: a dominant serotype and one or more minority serotypes.
Serotype-specific prevalence then depends on how such a carriage episode is
counted. **pneumoalloc** defines serotype-specific prevalence by
allocating each carriage episode among its serotypes, so that serotype
prevalences add up to overall carriage. It compares four allocation
approaches:

```{r}
library(pneumoalloc)
allocation_approaches()
```

The analysis follows three steps, as in the PCV10 Nha Trang analysis:

| Step | Question | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | How common are carriage and multiple serotype carriage? What types of multiple carriage occur? | `fit_carriage_states()`, `fit_multiple_types()` |
| 2 | Serotype-specific prevalence among all children | `fit_carriage(population = "all")`; comparator: `fit_presence()` |
| 3 | Serotype composition among children with multiple carriage | `fit_carriage(population = "multiple")` |
| 4 | Density among carriers: all pneumococci, PCV10 and non-PCV10 serotypes | `fit_density()` |

Every model standardises its estimates over the study population
(posterior g-computation): every child is set to each survey round, the
predictions are averaged over the children within each posterior draw, and
ratios between rounds are formed within the same draw.

## A worked example (Table S1)

`table_s1` is a hypothetical population of ten children, six of them
carriers:

```{r}
table_s1
ex <- prepare_carriage_data(
  table_s1, survey = "survey",
  serotypes = c("sero1", "sero2", "sero3"),
  abundance = c("ra1", "ra2", "ra3"),
  density = "density"
)
```

Each approach gives every carrier a contribution to each serotype. Child 6
carries 6B (relative abundance 0.5), 15A (0.3) and 23A (0.2):

```{r}
k6 <- which(ex$pos_idx == 6)
sapply(c("dominant", "equal", "abundance", "presence"),
       function(a) allocate_weights(ex, a)[k6, c("6B", "15A", "23A")])
```

Under the `density` approach the contributions are also weighted by the
child's density relative to the mean density of carriers. Prevalence of
PCV10 and non-PCV10 carriage, as numbers of the ten children:

```{r}
crude <- lapply(c("dominant", "equal", "abundance", "density", "presence"),
                function(a) describe_prevalence(ex, a))
totals <- sapply(crude, function(x) 10 * x$value[match(c("VT", "NVT", "Overall"), x$outcome)])
dimnames(totals) <- list(c("PCV10", "Non-PCV10", "Overall"),
                         c("dominant", "equal", "abundance", "density", "presence"))
round(totals, 3)
```

All four allocation approaches keep overall carriage at six children; the
presence-based approach counts children with both kinds of serotype twice.

## Preparing survey data

The data need one row per child: the survey round, one column per
detected-serotype slot, the relative abundance of each slot and total
density. `simulate_carriage_data()` makes an example with three rounds, the
first before vaccine introduction:

```{r}
sim <- simulate_carriage_data(seed = 1)
head(sim)
```

`prepare_carriage_data()` builds everything the models share. Rare
non-vaccine serotypes are pooled into "Other NVT", the reference category
of the composition model. Declare every covariate you may adjust for, so
that unadjusted and adjusted models use the same children, and choose the
reference (pre-vaccination) round for prevalence ratios.

```{r}
dat <- prepare_carriage_data(
  sim,
  survey = "survey",
  serotypes = c("sero1", "sero2", "sero3"),
  abundance = c("ra1", "ra2", "ra3"),
  density = "density",
  vaccine_types = pcv10_types(),
  categories = c(pcv10_types(), "6A", "15B/C", "19A", "11A", "35B"),
  covariates = c("age_z", "sex"),
  reference = "2016"
)
dat
```

Any set of serotypes can form the vaccine-type group (`vaccine_types()`
has the sets of PCV7 to PCV21 and PPSV23, with `add` and `remove`), any
number of covariates can be declared, and `max_serotypes` sets how many
serotypes per child the models distinguish (by default the largest number
detected, up to 5).

Crude estimates need no model:

```{r}
states <- describe_carriage_states(dat)
states[states$outcome %in% c("Carriage", "Multiple carriage"), ]
```

## Step 1: overall and multiple serotype carriage

`fit_carriage_states()` classifies each child by the number of detected
serotypes (none, one, two, three) in a multinomial-logit model.
`fit_multiple_types()` classifies children with multiple carriage as
VT-only, NVT-only, mixed VT-dominant or mixed NVT-dominant. Both take a
covariate formula for adjusted models (`NULL`, the default, fits the
unadjusted model):

```{r, eval = run_fits}
fit_states <- fit_carriage_states(dat, covariates = ~ age_z + sex, refresh = 0)
fit_types <- fit_multiple_types(dat, covariates = ~ age_z + sex, refresh = 0)

marginal_prevalence(fit_states, groups = c("carriage", "multiple"))
prevalence_ratios(fit_states, groups = c("carriage", "multiple"))
prevalence_ratios(fit_types)
```

By default, prevalence ratios compare each round with the reference round.
Use `reference = "previous"` to compare each round with the one before it,
or name any round:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
prevalence_ratios(fit_states, groups = "multiple", reference = "previous")
```

## Step 2: serotype-specific carriage among all children

`fit_carriage()` fits the unified framework: overall carriage (logistic),
serotype composition among carriers (fractional multinomial logit) and
density among carriers (lognormal with a sub-model for the number of
serotypes), jointly. The approaches differ only in the allocation weights,
so all fits share the population, design and priors. Choose the
approaches by the aim of the analysis: one approach (e.g.
`approach = "density"`), several (`c("dominant", "density")`), or
`"all"` (the default) to compare them. The defaults are 4 chains of
1000 warm-up and 2000 sampling iterations.

```{r, eval = run_fits}
fits <- fit_carriage(dat, approach = "all", covariates = ~ age_z + sex, refresh = 0)
fits
```

Estimates and ratios for PCV10 and non-PCV10 carriage, and for each
serotype:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
prev <- marginal_prevalence(fits$density, groups = c("overall", "VT", "NVT"))
prev[prev$measure == "prevalence", c("outcome", "survey", "estimate")]

pr <- prevalence_ratios(fits$density, groups = "serotype")
pr[pr$measure == "prevalence", c("outcome", "survey", "estimate", "reportable")]
```

Serotype ratios are flagged as not `reportable` when the reference-round
prevalence is close to zero.

Mean density among carriers, its ratio between rounds and the density
ratios by number of serotypes:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
density_ratios(fits$density, multiplicity = TRUE)
```

### Serotype groups within VT or NVT carriage

`group_proportions()` gives the share of a group of serotypes in
non-PCV10 (`among = "NVT"`), PCV10 (`"VT"`) or all carriage by survey
round, and its ratio between rounds, formed within each posterior draw:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
group_proportions(fits$density, list("15B/C+23A+35B" = c("15B/C", "23A", "35B")),
                  among = "NVT")
```

### The presence-based approach

Many carriage studies use a presence-based definition: a serotype counts
whenever it is detected, regardless of dominance, abundance or density.
`fit_presence()` fits it (an independent logistic model per outcome, on
the same design) for comparison. A child carrying both a PCV10 and a
non-PCV10 serotype counts for both, so the two prevalences can add up to
more than overall carriage. Add the fit to `compare_approaches()` to see
it next to the four allocation approaches:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
presence <- fit_presence(dat, covariates = ~ age_z + sex, refresh = 0)
cmp_all <- compare_approaches(c(fits, list(presence = presence)))
r <- cmp_all$ratios
r[r$group %in% c("VT", "NVT") & r$measure == "prevalence",
  c("method", "outcome", "survey", "estimate")]
```

## Step 3: serotype composition of multiple carriage

With `population = "multiple"` the same framework is fitted among children
with multiple carriage only. The estimand is the serotype composition of
multiple carriage, and the ratios are proportion ratios:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
fits_multi <- fit_carriage(dat, approach = "all", population = "multiple",
                           covariates = ~ age_z + sex, refresh = 0)
prevalence_ratios(fits_multi$density, groups = c("VT", "NVT"))
```

## Step 4: density among carriers

`fit_density()` fits lognormal regressions of density among carriers,
with effects for carrying at least two and at least three serotypes, for
all pneumococci (`"total"`) and for the PCV10 (`"VT"`) and non-PCV10
(`"NVT"`) serotypes. Group density is the sum of the serotype-specific
densities (total density times relative abundance) of the group's
serotypes. Observed densities first:

```{r}
describe_density(dat)
```

The model estimates the mean and the median density in each round, with
the observed number of serotypes held fixed; the column `statistic` says
which. Choose with `statistic`; the PCV10 Nha Trang analysis reports
median density ratios:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
dens <- fit_density(dat, covariates = ~ age_z + sex, refresh = 0)
density_ratios(dens, statistic = "median", multiplicity = TRUE)
```

`interaction = TRUE` lets the multiplicity effects differ by survey round
and also returns their ratio to the reference round:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
dens_int <- fit_density(dat, group = "total", interaction = TRUE,
                        covariates = ~ age_z + sex, refresh = 0)
density_ratios(dens_int, statistic = "median", multiplicity = TRUE)
```

`fit_carriage()` also models total density, as part of the unified
framework; there the mean density is marginalised over the predicted
number of serotypes (`marginal_density(fits$density)`).

## Figures

Each plotting function returns a ggplot object, which can be modified,
combined or saved with `ggplot2::ggsave()`:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
plot_carriage_states(fit_states)
plot_prevalence(c(fits, list(presence = presence)))
plot_ratios(fits)
plot_density(dens)
plot_serotypes(fits[c("dominant", "density")])
plot_serotype_ratios(fits[c("dominant", "density")])
```

## Checking fits and comparing approaches

`check_fit()` reports sampler diagnostics, R-hat and ESS of the parameters
and estimates, identities that must hold in every draw, and the comparison
with the crude estimates (close for unadjusted models):

```{r, eval = run_fits}
check_fit(fits$density)
```

`compare_approaches()` checks that overall carriage, multiplicity and
density, which do not depend on the allocation, agree across approaches
within Monte Carlo error, and binds the estimates of all approaches for
tables and figures:

```{r, eval = run_fits}
cmp <- compare_approaches(fits)
summary(cmp$shared$z)
vt_nvt <- cmp$ratios[cmp$ratios$group %in% c("VT", "NVT") & cmp$ratios$measure == "prevalence", ]
vt_nvt[, c("method", "outcome", "survey", "estimate")]
```

Save fits with `save_fit()` (draws otherwise live in temporary files) and
write all tables to Excel with `write_results()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
save_fit(fits, "fits_adjusted.rds")
write_results(fits, "results_adjusted.xlsx")
```

## A quick test

A script that runs every model on simulated data with short chains, and
prints the main results and checks, is installed with the package:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
source(system.file("scripts", "quick_test.R", package = "pneumoalloc"))
```

## Priors

The default priors are those of the PCV10 Nha Trang analysis. Prior scales
are passed to Stan as data, so changing them needs no recompilation:

```{r}
carriage_priors()
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fit_carriage(dat, approach = "density", priors = carriage_priors(share = 5))
```

## Run time

The unified model is implemented with Stan's GLM functions and a
precomputed composition term: the same model as the Stan file of the PCV10
Nha Trang analysis (log densities equal to floating-point rounding), but
several times faster. Within-chain threads do not speed it up: keep
`threads_per_chain = 1` (the default) and give each chain its own core.

## Running on a computing cluster

Each fit is independent, so approaches and models can run as separate jobs
(for example one Slurm array task per approach). Compile once with
`carriage_model(model, dir = "<shared directory>")` and pass the result
to the fitting functions as `model`. Parallelism comes from chains
(`parallel_chains`).
